title: Simulation I: The Complete Set
prompt:
**Task.** A string of n lowercase letters; the alphabet is exactly the
k distinct letters that appear (given as k). Find the length of the
shortest contiguous substring containing all k distinct letters at least
once each. Print that length, or −1 if impossible.

**Constraints:** 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ k ≤ 26 (with k = number of distinct
letters in the string, so −1 cannot actually occur — decide for yourself
whether to trust that).

tests.name: warmup
tests.hint: bca (or cab) covers all 3 letters in length 3.

tests.name: whole string
tests.hint: Both endpoints occur exactly once — every proper window loses a letter.

tests.name: single letters
interleaved
tests.hint: Sweep-verified in Python (this input also defeats chunk-greedy scans).

tests.name: full scale
tests.hint: n = 200000 over 3 letters: the honest two-pointer sweep is O(n). Ground truth in Python.
